question: What nomenclatural changes or source-name conflicts appear when the 2014 Tikub Lake survey labels are compared with the current Catalogue of Life Extended Release?

sourceContext.bibliography: Labatos, B. V. Jr., and Briones, N. D. (2014). Freshwater Fishes of Tikub Lake, Tiaong, Quezon, Philippines. Asian Journal of Biodiversity, 5(1), 41-53. https://doi.org/10.7828/ajob.v5i1.480
sourceContext.accessAndRights: The public author upload displays a copyright warning. No item-specific license or permission for the checklist was identified. This review records only a minimal set of nomenclatural deltas and does not reproduce either source table.
sourceContext.sourceSeparation: The article distinguishes nine collected taxa from four additional reported-only taxa. Those evidence classes remain separate; a checklist name match does not change either class.

taxonomyReference.provider: Catalogue of Life via ChecklistBank API
limits: Catalogue of Life name matching proposes nomenclatural mappings; it does not validate the 2014 authors' specimens or identifications.
Checklist content and match results can change between releases; these values are pinned to the stated 2026-10-16 XR dataset.
No occurrence search or distribution inference was performed in this crosswalk.

crosswalkFindings.summary: Of the 13 collected-or-reported source taxa, nine names matched accepted species-rank usages without a changed species name, three collected source labels returned synonym usages mapping to accepted species names, and the red-tilapia hybrid remains unresolved because the abstract and table disagree on one parent label. A separate parent-name match maps Oreochromis hornorum to Oreochromis urolepis; that synonym does not determine the identity of the reported hybrid.

sourceNameDeltas.decision: Preserve the source spelling in the historical record; retain the CoL XR candidate as a nomenclatural crosswalk only.
Preserve the source trinomial; do not promote the source identification or imply that the checklist resolved specimen identity.
Preserve the source trinomial; this is a nomenclatural mapping and not a verification of the specimens.

hybridConflict.decision: Do not resolve the hybrid to either parent combination or treat it as an independently identified species. Preserve the abstract/table discrepancy and source term.

crosswalkFindings.reportedOnlyDisposition: The four taxa that the article lists as reported rather than collected remain in that separate source category. Their nomenclatural matches do not turn them into survey captures or site-level occurrence rows.

reuseAndEvidenceDecision.reason: The crosswalk resolves only three synonym-name deltas and documents one hybrid-parent conflict. The article's item-specific reuse terms remain unverified, the species tables were not copied, and CoL XR cannot validate the source specimens, locality assignments, survey recency, or collection status.

nextAction: Seek item-specific reuse clarification for the 2014 article before considering any source-derived occurrence rows. Keep the collected-versus-reported distinction, original name labels, hybrid discrepancy, and historical survey date explicit; do not infer current presence or lake-wide completeness.
